items.stem: In Airflow, what does a DAG file primarily do?

options.text: Defines the structure, schedule and dependencies of tasks; the work runs in task execution
options.rationale: Correct: the DAG file is a definition parsed by the scheduler, not where the work executes.

options.text: Executes all the data processing at parse time
options.rationale: Heavy work belongs in task execution, not DAG parsing.
Output goes to external systems, not the DAG file.
The metadata database is separate from DAG definitions.

items.explanation: Correct: the DAG file is a definition parsed by the scheduler, not where the work executes.

items.stem: Which practices improve Airflow pipeline reliability? (Select TWO)

options.text: Making tasks idempotent so re-runs produce the same result
options.rationale: Correct: idempotency makes retries and backfills safe.

options.text: Using deferrable sensors to wait without occupying a worker slot
options.rationale: Correct: deferrable sensors free worker capacity while waiting.

options.text: Pushing large datasets through XCom between tasks
options.rationale: XCom is for small values; large data belongs in external storage.

options.text: Setting unlimited retries on every task
options.rationale: Unlimited retries mask genuine failures and waste resources.

items.explanation: Correct: idempotency makes retries and backfills safe.; Correct: deferrable sensors free worker capacity while waiting.

items.stem: What does a task's data interval (logical date) represent?

options.text: The period of data the run is responsible for processing
options.rationale: Correct: the data interval identifies which slice of data the run covers.

options.text: The exact wall-clock time the task started
options.rationale: That is the real start time, not the data interval.

options.text: The time the DAG file was last edited
options.rationale: Editing time is unrelated to the data interval.
Retry count is separate from the data interval.

items.explanation: Correct: the data interval identifies which slice of data the run covers.
